// expected: CLEAN
// agentapp: the enterprise agent layer, first lifecycle: Define (LIFECYCLE.md). An enterprise agent does not answer to
// one user's chat. A teammate submits an intent on a document; the document's gate decides whether a run may start
// (the PRD is locked until the MRD is accepted, and one run at a time writes a document); the run works in isolation,
// reports to the intent, and publishes a version only after a grant. A grant comes from the intent's owner, or from
// the owner's policy for that action class, read before the run starts. Only a person accepts a document.
// Personal agents (server/personal.mjs) act through these same machines: they submit, queue, approve and answer as
// their person's preferences allow, and every one of those steps is checked here, not assumed.
// Machines hold addresses, not each other's state, and talk only by send, so the configuration checks them with
// messages arriving in any order.
module agentapp

enum IntentState { Draft, Claiming, Working, Asking, Delivered, Accepted, Rejected, Refused, Queued, Failed, Cancelled }

enum RunState { Idle, Working, Waiting, Blocked, Suspended, Publishing, Done, Failed, Stopped, Closed }

// Why the runtime stopped a run: it asked for more model calls than its step limit, or spent past its cost budget.
enum StopReason { Running, StepLimit, CostBudget }

enum DocState { Open, Drafted, Accepted }

// An obligation is what a person owes another: a document, by a date. A plan is one way to meet it and can change; the
// obligation stays. Open is on track. Met, Missed and Released end it.
enum ObligationState { Open, AtRisk, Met, Missed, Released }

// Where a grant came from. ByPerson is a person's answer; ByPolicy is the owner's preference for the action class,
// fixed on the intent before it was submitted.
enum GrantSource { NoGrant, ByPerson, ByPolicy }

// Intent: what a teammate asked for, and the team's side of the conversation with the agent.
machine Intent {
  state {
    st          : IntentState   = Draft
    run         : Ref<Run>      = none
    doc         : Ref<Document> = none
    approved    : bool          = false
    heard       : bool          = false
    // the owner's preferences for this intent's action classes: publish (or post findings) without asking, and
    // queue a refused intent without asking. SetPolicy is accepted only in Draft, so the run never starts under a
    // policy other than the one it was submitted with.
    autoPublish : bool          = false
    autoQueue   : bool          = false
    // the last grant this intent sent its run, and whether it has ever been queued (a queued intent is queued once)
    grant       : GrantSource   = NoGrant
    queued      : bool          = false
    // the obligation this intent works toward: every intent belongs to exactly one, wired when it is created. A
    // configuration that does not model obligations leaves it none, and the intent then reports to nobody.
    obligation  : Ref<Obligation> = none
  }

  terminal st in { Accepted, Rejected, Failed, Cancelled }

  action SetPolicy(publish: bool, queue: bool)
  action Submit()
  action Cancel()
  action Claimed()
  action Refused()
  action Queue()
  action Bumped()
  action Wake()
  action Dequeue()
  action Drop()
  action Progress()
  action PermissionAsked()
  action Approve()
  action Deny()
  action Finished()
  action RunFailed()
  action Accept()
  action Reject()

  on SetPolicy(publish, queue) {
    require st == Draft else reject "submitted"
    autoPublish' = publish
    autoQueue' = queue
  }

  // The document's gate decides, not the intent: a locked or busy document refuses the claim.
  on Submit {
    require st == Draft else reject "not-draft"
    st' = Claiming
    send doc <- Claim(from: self, worker: run)
  }

  // A cancelled draft closes its run, which would otherwise wait for a start forever (PL5402).
  on Cancel {
    require st == Draft else reject "submitted"
    st' = Cancelled
    send run <- Close()
  }

  on Claimed {
    require st == Claiming else reject "not-claiming"
    st' = Working
  }

  // A refusal is not the end: the owner (or the owner's policy) may queue the intent on the document, which wakes it
  // when the gate opens. Its run stays Idle until then; Drop closes it.
  on Refused {
    require st == Claiming else reject "not-claiming"
    if autoQueue && !queued {
      st' = Queued
      queued' = true
      send doc <- Enqueue(from: self)
    } else {
      st' = Refused
    }
  }

  on Queue {
    require st == Refused && !queued else reject "not-queueable"
    st' = Queued
    queued' = true
    send doc <- Enqueue(from: self)
  }

  // The document's one queue slot was taken: the intent is refused again and may be dropped.
  on Bumped {
    require st == Queued else reject "not-queued"
    st' = Refused
  }

  // The document woke the queue: claim it again. `started` marks the start for the path property below; a queued
  // intent is queued once (queued), so it is woken at most once.
  on Wake {
    require st == Queued else reject "not-queued"
    st' = Claiming
    emit started()
    send doc <- Claim(from: self, worker: run)
  }

  // The undo of a queue. A Wake already in transit reaches a cancelled intent and is refused.
  on Dequeue {
    require st == Queued else reject "not-queued"
    st' = Cancelled
    send doc <- Dequeue(from: self)
    send run <- Close()
  }

  on Drop {
    require st == Refused else reject "not-refused"
    st' = Cancelled
    send run <- Close()
  }

  // A report may arrive before Claimed, or after a permission request sent later, so it never moves the intent back.
  on Progress {
    require st == Claiming || st == Working || st == Asking || st == Delivered else reject "not-running"
    heard' = true
  }

  // The run asks to publish. The owner's policy grants it at once; otherwise the owner is asked. A run granted by
  // policy is never sent back (Deny needs Asking), so it asks once; a second request is refused.
  on PermissionAsked {
    require st == Claiming || st == Working else reject "not-running"
    require !autoPublish || grant == NoGrant else reject "already-granted"
    if autoPublish {
      st' = Working
      grant' = ByPolicy
      send run <- Granted(by: ByPolicy)
    } else {
      st' = Asking
    }
  }

  on Approve {
    require st == Asking else reject "not-asking"
    st' = Working
    approved' = true
    grant' = ByPerson
    send run <- Granted(by: ByPerson)
  }

  on Deny {
    require st == Asking else reject "not-asking"
    st' = Working
    send run <- Denied()
  }

  on Finished {
    require st == Claiming || st == Working else reject "not-working"
    st' = Delivered
    if obligation != none {
      send obligation <- Deliver()
    }
  }

  on RunFailed {
    require st == Claiming || st == Working || st == Asking else reject "not-running"
    st' = Failed
    if obligation != none {
      send obligation <- Stall()
    }
  }

  on Accept {
    require st == Delivered else reject "not-delivered"
    st' = Accepted
  }

  on Reject {
    require st == Delivered else reject "not-delivered"
    st' = Rejected
    if obligation != none {
      send obligation <- Rework()
    }
  }

  invariant policy-grant-needs-the-policy: grant == ByPolicy implies autoPublish
  invariant person-grant-was-approved: grant == ByPerson implies approved
  path property queued-starts-at-most-once: count("intent.start") <= 1

  // A marker, not an action on the world: the host records it in the activity log. It lets the path property count
  // wakes.
  effect started() {
    kind "intent.start"
    labels { write:store }
    class none
  }
}

// Document: an MRD or a PRD, and its gate. A service: it lives as long as the project, so it has no terminal state
// (PS1.7). A gated document (the PRD) takes a claim only while its upstream document is accepted: Unlock arrives
// when that document is accepted, Relock when it is reopened.
service machine Document {
  state {
    st         : DocState       = Open
    gated      : bool           = false
    ready      : bool           = false
    busy       : bool           = false
    drafted    : bool           = false
    // the downstream document has not yet acknowledged the last Unlock or Relock; bounds what is in transit
    pending    : bool           = false
    down       : Ref<Document>  = none
    // one intent waiting for the gate to open (a one-slot queue; a second is bumped)
    queued     : Ref<Intent>    = none
    acceptedBy : GrantSource    = NoGrant
    // the obligation to deliver this document: a person's acceptance of it is what meets that obligation
    owed       : Ref<Obligation> = none
  }

  action Unlock(from: Ref<Document>)
  action Relock(from: Ref<Document>)
  action Acked()
  action Claim(from: Ref<Intent>, worker: Ref<Run>)
  action Enqueue(from: Ref<Intent>)
  action Dequeue(from: Ref<Intent>)
  action Published()
  action Released()
  action Unpublish(last: bool)
  action Accept(by: GrantSource)
  action Reopen()

  // The queue wakes here, on the gated document, when Unlock arrives, and not from the upstream document when it is
  // accepted. Messages arrive in any order: had the MRD woken the queued PRD intent itself, the intent's Claim could
  // reach the PRD before the MRD's Unlock did, and the gate would refuse it a second time. Waking on Unlock means the
  // gate is already open when the Claim is sent.
  on Unlock(from) {
    require gated else reject "not-gated"
    ready' = true
    send from <- Acked()
    if queued != none && !busy && st != Accepted {
      queued' = none
      send queued <- Wake()
    }
  }

  on Relock(from) {
    require gated else reject "not-gated"
    ready' = false
    send from <- Acked()
  }

  on Acked {
    require pending else reject "not-pending"
    pending' = false
  }

  on Claim(from, worker) {
    require true else reject "never"
    if st != Accepted && !busy && (!gated || ready) {
      busy' = true
      send worker <- Start(from: from, doc: self)
      send from <- Claimed()
    } else {
      send from <- Refused()
    }
  }

  // Queued while the gate is already open: wake it at once. Otherwise hold it in the slot, or bump it if taken.
  on Enqueue(from) {
    require true else reject "never"
    if st != Accepted && !busy && (!gated || ready) {
      send from <- Wake()
    } else {
      if queued == none {
        queued' = from
      } else {
        send from <- Bumped()
      }
    }
  }

  // A Dequeue for an intent the queue already woke (or bumped) finds the slot not holding it, and is refused.
  on Dequeue(from) {
    require queued == from else reject "not-queued-here"
    queued' = none
  }

  // A version is published by the run that holds the document; an Accepted document is reopened first.
  on Published {
    require busy else reject "not-busy"
    busy' = false
    drafted' = true
    st' = Drafted
    if queued != none && (!gated || ready) {
      queued' = none
      send queued <- Wake()
    }
  }

  on Released {
    require busy else reject "not-busy"
    busy' = false
    if queued != none && st != Accepted && (!gated || ready) {
      queued' = none
      send queued <- Wake()
    }
  }

  // The undo of a version published by policy. Taking back the last version leaves nothing to accept.
  on Unpublish(last) {
    require st == Drafted && !busy else reject "not-unpublishable"
    if last {
      st' = Open
      drafted' = false
    } else {
      drafted' = true
    }
  }

  // Only a person accepts, and only a drafted document that no run is writing. A policy never accepts.
  on Accept(by) {
    require by == ByPerson else reject "needs-a-person"
    require st == Drafted && !busy && !pending else reject "not-acceptable"
    st' = Accepted
    acceptedBy' = by
    if down != none {
      pending' = true
      send down <- Unlock(from: self)
    }
    // the obligation is told once: a later acceptance of a reopened document is for a later obligation
    if owed != none {
      send owed <- Confirm(by: by)
      owed' = none
    }
  }

  // An intent queued while the document was accepted waits for it to be reopened: Reopen opens the gate, so it wakes
  // the queue as Unlock does.
  on Reopen {
    require st == Accepted && !pending else reject "not-reopenable"
    st' = Drafted
    if down != none {
      pending' = true
      send down <- Relock(from: self)
    }
    if queued != none && !busy && (!gated || ready) {
      queued' = none
      send queued <- Wake()
    }
  }

  invariant accepted-was-drafted: st == Accepted implies drafted
  invariant accepted-by-a-person: st == Accepted implies acceptedBy == ByPerson
  // A document that would take a claim holds no queued intent: every step that opens the gate (Unlock, Reopen, the
  // end of a run) wakes the queue. Before Reopen woke it, an intent queued on an accepted document stayed queued
  // after a reopen; this invariant fails on that program.
  invariant queue-empty-while-claimable: (st != Accepted && !busy && (!gated || ready)) implies queued == none
}

// Person: a teammate's address, so a run can ask a decision of a named person and not only of its owner. The question
// arrives here as a message (the host turns it into a card in the person's inbox); the answer is the person's input
// on the run, which takes it only from the person it asked.
service machine Person {
  state {
    asked : bool = false
    // an obligation of this person's was reported at risk or missed
    told  : bool = false
  }

  action Asked(from: Ref<Run>)
  action Told(from: Ref<Obligation>)

  on Asked(from) {
    require true else reject "never"
    asked' = true
  }

  on Told(from) {
    require true else reject "never"
    told' = true
  }
}

// Obligation: what the debtor owes the creditor, and whether it is being met. The plan that meets it lives in the intents
// and can change; this machine does not. Messages from the intents and the document arrive in any order, so each
// handler is total: a report that finds the obligation already ended changes nothing.
// working: a run is on it. asked: a person has been asked something that moves it (the plan, a path to choose, or
// the confirmation of a delivery). An obligation that is Open or AtRisk always has one of the two.
service machine Obligation {
  state {
    st         : ObligationState = Open
    debtor     : Ref<Person>     = none
    creditor   : Ref<Person>     = none
    // the debtor is asked to approve the plan first
    working    : bool            = false
    asked      : bool            = true
    delivered  : bool            = false
    accepted   : bool            = false
    acceptedBy : GrantSource     = NoGrant
    // the creditor and the debtor have been told the obligation is at risk or missed
    told       : bool            = false
    // it was at risk and went back on track by another path
    rerouted   : bool            = false
    // how many times the debtor changed the path, and how many times the configuration lets them. The limit is a
    // parameter and not a rule of the product: the host sets it high, and a configuration sets it small so the check
    // stays exhaustive (the transit bound). The checked range is small; the host's is not.
    reroutes   : int check 0..2  = 0
    maxReroutes: int check 0..2  = 2
    // a report reached the obligation after it had ended; it changed nothing (a write, so the no-op is visible)
    late       : bool            = false
    // a sub-obligation names the obligation it is part of. It goes at risk only when its parent has: the parent
    // hears the doubt first (ChildDoubt) and passes it on (Warn), so no state has a child at risk and its parent on track.
    parent     : Ref<Obligation> = none
  }

  action Go()
  action Doubt()
  action Reroute()
  action Deliver()
  action Stall()
  action Rework()
  action Confirm(by: GrantSource)
  action Lapse()
  action Release()
  action ChildDoubt(from: Ref<Obligation>, ack: Ref<Order>)
  action Warn(ack: Ref<Order>)
  action Back(ack: Ref<Order>)
  action Cleared(ack: Ref<Order>)

  // The plan was approved: a run starts.
  on Go {
    require st == Open && asked && !working && !delivered else reject "not-waiting-for-the-plan"
    working' = true
    asked' = false
  }

  // A reason to expect the date will be missed (the person who must answer is away): at risk, and the debtor and the
  // creditor are told. The run, if any, keeps its place; the debtor is asked for a path.
  on Doubt {
    require st == Open && parent == none && reroutes < maxReroutes else reject "not-on-track"
    st' = AtRisk
    asked' = true
    told' = true
    if creditor != none {
      send creditor <- Told(from: self)
    }
    if debtor != none {
      send debtor <- Told(from: self)
    }
  }

  // The debtor chose another path: back on track, with a run on it.
  on Reroute {
    require st == AtRisk && asked && reroutes < maxReroutes else reject "not-at-risk"
    st' = Open
    working' = true
    asked' = false
    rerouted' = true
    reroutes' = reroutes + 1
  }

  // The run delivered the document: the creditor is asked to confirm it.
  on Deliver {
    require true else reject "never"
    if st == Open || st == AtRisk {
      working' = false
      asked' = true
      delivered' = true
    } else {
      late' = true
    }
  }

  // The run failed or stopped. Nothing is working on it any more: it is at risk and the debtor is asked for a path.
  on Stall {
    require true else reject "never"
    if st == Open && parent == none {
      st' = AtRisk
      working' = false
      asked' = true
      told' = true
      if creditor != none {
        send creditor <- Told(from: self)
      }
      if debtor != none {
        send debtor <- Told(from: self)
      }
    } else {
      if st == AtRisk {
        working' = false
        asked' = true
      } else {
        late' = true
      }
    }
  }

  // The delivery was sent back: a new run works on it.
  on Rework {
    require true else reject "never"
    if st == Open || st == AtRisk {
      working' = true
      asked' = false
      delivered' = false
    } else {
      late' = true
    }
  }

  // The document it owes was accepted. Only a person's acceptance meets an obligation; the document refuses any other
  // source before this message is sent.
  on Confirm(by) {
    require by == ByPerson else reject "needs-a-person"
    if st == Open || st == AtRisk {
      st' = Met
      working' = false
      asked' = false
      accepted' = true
      acceptedBy' = by
    } else {
      late' = true
    }
  }

  // The date passed with the obligation not met: both parties are told, with the reason from the record.
  on Lapse {
    require st == Open || st == AtRisk else reject "ended"
    st' = Missed
    told' = true
    if creditor != none {
      send creditor <- Told(from: self)
    }
    if debtor != none {
      send debtor <- Told(from: self)
    }
  }

  on Release {
    require st == Open || st == AtRisk else reject "ended"
    st' = Released
    working' = false
    asked' = false
  }

  // A part of this obligation has a reason to doubt its date. This obligation goes at risk first, the debtor is asked
  // for a path, and the part is told to follow (Warn). Whoever raised the doubt (ack) hears back once the part has
  // followed, and only then lets anyone choose a path: a choice made earlier could be overtaken by the warning.
  // Total: the parent may already be at risk or ended.
  on ChildDoubt(from, ack) {
    require true else reject "never"
    if st == Open {
      st' = AtRisk
      asked' = true
      told' = true
      if creditor != none {
        send creditor <- Told(from: self)
      }
      if debtor != none {
        send debtor <- Told(from: self)
      }
      send from <- Warn(ack: ack)
    } else {
      if st == AtRisk {
        send from <- Warn(ack: ack)
      } else {
        late' = true
        if ack != none {
          send ack <- Warned()
        }
      }
    }
  }

  // A part is back on track: the debtor chose another path and the order says so (Back). The part first, then this
  // obligation, so no state has a part at risk and its parent on track. Whoever asked (ack) hears when it is all done, and
  // starts nothing new before: a doubt that overtook the clearing would leave a part at risk under a parent on track.
  // Total, like the doubt: the part may not be at risk, or may not be rerouted again (the host sets how many times).
  on Back(ack) {
    require true else reject "never"
    if st == AtRisk && reroutes < maxReroutes {
      st' = Open
      working' = true
      asked' = false
      rerouted' = true
      reroutes' = reroutes + 1
      if parent != none {
        send parent <- Cleared(ack: ack)
      } else {
        if ack != none {
          send ack <- Warned()
        }
      }
    } else {
      late' = true
      if ack != none {
        send ack <- Warned()
      }
    }
  }

  // The part is back on track, so this obligation is, if it has no other reason to be at risk. A parent that cannot be
  // rerouted again stays at risk.
  on Cleared(ack) {
    require true else reject "never"
    if st == AtRisk && reroutes < maxReroutes {
      st' = Open
      working' = true
      asked' = false
      rerouted' = true
      reroutes' = reroutes + 1
    } else {
      late' = true
    }
    if ack != none {
      send ack <- Warned()
    }
  }

  // The parent is at risk, so this part is too. Only a parent's message puts a part at risk. The answer goes back to
  // whoever raised the doubt, whatever became of this part.
  on Warn(ack) {
    require true else reject "never"
    if st == Open && parent != none {
      st' = AtRisk
      asked' = true
      told' = true
      if creditor != none {
        send creditor <- Told(from: self)
      }
      if debtor != none {
        send debtor <- Told(from: self)
      }
    } else {
      late' = true
    }
    if ack != none {
      send ack <- Warned()
    }
  }

  invariant open-has-someone: (st == Open || st == AtRisk) implies (working || asked)
  invariant met-was-accepted-by-a-person: st == Met implies (accepted && acceptedBy == ByPerson)
  invariant at-risk-and-missed-were-told: (st == AtRisk || st == Missed) implies told
  invariant rerouted-came-from-at-risk: rerouted implies told
}

// Run: one isolated agent run for one intent on one document. Its own work (Step, Ready, Fail) is its input; it
// reports each step and blocks before it publishes a version until the intent grants it.
// Model calls are metered here, not in the host: the model gateway asks CallRequested before every call and reports
// CallCompleted(cost) after it, and the run stops itself (Stopped) when it asks past its step limit or has spent its
// cost budget. Cost is in micro-dollars. A server restart interrupts a run (Suspended) and does not fail it: Resume
// returns it to Working, so the document stays held by the same run and the host continues from the run's checkpoint.
// A run that needs a decision asks a named person (Ask) and waits (Waiting) until that person answers or declines.
machine Run {
  state {
    st         : RunState      = Idle
    owner      : Ref<Intent>   = none
    target     : Ref<Document> = none
    reported   : bool          = false
    granted    : bool          = false
    published  : bool          = false
    grant      : GrantSource   = NoGrant
    // the person the run is waiting on, and who answered its last question
    asked      : Ref<Person>   = none
    answeredBy : Ref<Person>   = none
    // how many questions the run has asked, and how many it may ask: a run interrupts people a bounded number of
    // times. Set by the host like the step limit; the checked range is small, the host's may be larger.
    questions  : int check 0..2 = 0
    maxAsk     : int check 0..2 = 1
    // metering, set by the host when the run is created (config per role, defaults in server/limits.mjs). The checked
    // ranges are small so the check stays exhaustive; the host counts in micro-dollars, far outside them. The
    // comparisons are linear, so what is checked is their shape, and the cost domain is disclosed (PT3.4) rather than
    // strict: the runtime accepts a cost outside 0..8 (the host keeps no drift journal).
    calls      : int check 0..4 = 0
    limit      : int check 0..4 = 1
    spent      : int check 0..16 = 0
    budget     : int check 0..8 = 1
    stop       : StopReason     = Running
  }

  terminal st in { Done, Failed, Stopped, Closed }

  action Start(from: Ref<Intent>, doc: Ref<Document>)
  action Step()
  action Ready()
  action Granted(by: GrantSource)
  action Denied()
  action Published()
  action PublishFailed()
  action Fail()
  action Close()
  action Ask(to: Ref<Person>)
  action Answered(by: Ref<Person>)
  action Unanswered(by: Ref<Person>)
  action CallRequested()
  action CallCompleted(cost: int check 0..8 disclosed)
  action Interrupted()
  action Resume()

  on Start(from, doc) {
    require st == Idle else reject "started"
    st' = Working
    owner' = from
    target' = doc
  }

  // The first report. Later progress notes are the host's activity log, not machine steps, so transit stays bounded.
  on Step {
    require st == Working && !reported else reject "reported"
    reported' = true
    send owner <- Progress()
  }

  on Ready {
    require st == Working && reported else reject "not-ready"
    st' = Blocked
    send owner <- PermissionAsked()
  }

  // The grant names its source; a run publishes only on a grant that has one.
  on Granted(by) {
    require st == Blocked else reject "not-blocked"
    require by != NoGrant else reject "no-grant"
    st' = Publishing
    granted' = true
    grant' = by
    emit publish()
  }

  on Denied {
    require st == Blocked else reject "not-blocked"
    st' = Working
  }

  // A role needs a decision it may not make: the run asks the person who owns it and holds the document meanwhile.
  on Ask(to) {
    require st == Working else reject "not-working"
    require to != none else reject "no-person"
    require questions < maxAsk else reject "too-many-questions"
    st' = Waiting
    questions' = questions + 1
    asked' = to
    answeredBy' = none
    send to <- Asked(from: self)
  }

  // Only the person asked can answer. Anyone else's answer is refused and the run keeps waiting.
  on Answered(by) {
    require st == Waiting else reject "not-waiting"
    require by == asked else reject "not-asked-of-you"
    st' = Working
    answeredBy' = by
  }

  // The person declined (or the question was cancelled for them): the run continues with the card's default.
  on Unanswered(by) {
    require st == Waiting else reject "not-waiting"
    require by == asked else reject "not-asked-of-you"
    st' = Working
  }

  on Published {
    require st == Publishing else reject "not-publishing"
    st' = Done
    published' = true
    send target <- Published()
    send owner <- Finished()
  }

  on PublishFailed {
    require st == Publishing else reject "not-publishing"
    st' = Failed
    send target <- Released()
    send owner <- RunFailed()
  }

  on Fail {
    require st == Working || st == Blocked || st == Waiting else reject "not-running"
    st' = Failed
    send target <- Released()
    send owner <- RunFailed()
  }

  on Close {
    require st == Idle else reject "started"
    st' = Closed
  }

  // The gateway asks before each model call. A refusal to proceed is the run stopping itself and telling its owner.
  on CallRequested {
    require st == Working else reject "not-working"
    if calls >= limit {
      st' = Stopped
      stop' = StepLimit
      send target <- Released()
      send owner <- RunFailed()
    } else {
      if spent >= budget {
        st' = Stopped
        stop' = CostBudget
        send target <- Released()
        send owner <- RunFailed()
      } else {
        calls' = calls + 1
      }
    }
  }

  // The gateway reports what the call cost. A call that takes the run past its budget stops it.
  on CallCompleted(cost) {
    require st == Working else reject "not-working"
    spent' = spent + cost
    if spent + cost > budget {
      st' = Stopped
      stop' = CostBudget
      send target <- Released()
      send owner <- RunFailed()
    }
  }

  // The server went away under a working run. The run keeps its document and waits for Resume. A waiting run has
  // nothing in flight, so a restart leaves it Waiting.
  on Interrupted {
    require st == Working else reject "not-working"
    st' = Suspended
  }

  on Resume {
    require st == Suspended else reject "not-suspended"
    st' = Working
  }

  invariant published-was-granted: published implies granted
  invariant publish-needs-a-grant: published implies grant != NoGrant
  invariant answer-came-from-the-asked: answeredBy == none || answeredBy == asked
  invariant questions-within-limit: questions <= maxAsk
  invariant calls-within-limit: calls <= limit
  invariant spent-within-budget-unless-stopped: spent <= budget || st == Stopped
  invariant stopped-has-a-reason: st == Stopped implies stop != Running
  path property publish-at-most-once: count("agent.publish") <= 1

  effect publish() {
    kind "agent.publish"
    labels { egress:external }
    class irreversible
    ok -> Published()
    failed -> PublishFailed()
  }
}

// ---- Order fulfilment: the same front door for operational work (README, "Orders"). -------------------------------
// An order is a saga: reserve the stock, pick, book a carrier pickup, hand the goods over, invoice, charge, and the
// customer confirms the receipt. Each step that took something has the step that gives it back (compensation). The
// order owes its customer a delivery, and that is an Obligation: the warehouse, the carrier booking and finance are
// sub-obligations of it. Quantities and money are counted in small ranges so the check is exhaustive; the host counts
// in units and cents, outside them, and the action parameters that carry them are disclosed (PT3.4) for that reason.

enum OrderState { Placed, Reserving, Short, Offering, Substituting, Picking, Booking, Rebooking, Unknown, Booked, Invoicing, Approving, Charging, Delivering, Done, Cancelled, Stuck }

// How a shortage was settled: the units ordered, the units of another model, a second shipment, a later date.
enum ShortPath { Direct, ViaSubstitute, ViaSplit, ViaMove }

// Stock: the units of one model in one warehouse. Orders share it. A reservation takes what is there, up to the
// quantity asked, and says how many it took; a release gives units back; a restock is units arriving.
service machine Stock {
  state {
    onHand      : int check 0..4 = 1
    // units out on reservations, and units that arrived since the start; the host allows as many arrivals as it likes,
    // the check allows maxReceived
    out         : int check 0..4 = 0
    received    : int check 0..2 = 0
    maxReceived : int check 0..2 = 2
  }

  action Reserve(from: Ref<Order>, qty: int check 0..2 disclosed, substitute: bool)
  action Release(n: int check 0..2 disclosed)
  action Restock(n: int check 0..2 disclosed)

  on Reserve(from, qty, substitute) {
    require qty > 0 else reject "nothing-asked"
    if onHand >= qty {
      onHand' = onHand - qty
      out' = out + qty
      if substitute {
        send from <- Substituted(got: qty)
      } else {
        send from <- Reserved(got: qty)
      }
    } else {
      onHand' = 0
      out' = out + onHand
      if substitute {
        send from <- Substituted(got: onHand)
      } else {
        send from <- Reserved(got: onHand)
      }
    }
  }

  // Only units that are out come back: a release of units never reserved is refused.
  on Release(n) {
    require n > 0 && n <= out else reject "nothing-reserved"
    onHand' = onHand + n
    out' = out - n
  }

  on Restock(n) {
    require n > 0 && received + n <= maxReceived else reject "nothing-arrived"
    onHand' = onHand + n
    received' = received + n
  }
}

machine Order {
  state {
    st           : OrderState  = Placed
    path         : ShortPath   = Direct
    stock        : Ref<Stock>  = none
    spare        : Ref<Stock>  = none
    // the main obligation and its parts: the warehouse owes the units picked, the carrier booking a pickup slot, finance
    // an invoice and a charge, each once
    main         : Ref<Obligation> = none
    pick         : Ref<Obligation> = none
    book         : Ref<Obligation> = none
    bill         : Ref<Obligation> = none
    qty          : int check 0..2 = 0
    // units reserved from the model ordered and from the substitute. A second shipment (a split) is the host's: it
    // places a new order for the units left over.
    held         : int check 0..2 = 0
    held2        : int check 0..2 = 0
    // the units of the substitute model the customer agreed to take: the order never holds more of it than that
    agreedX2     : int check 0..2 = 0
    // some units were cancelled at the customer's request
    trimmed      : bool        = false
    // money: a charge above the limit, or to a new customer, needs a person's approval. The host passes the amount
    // each time it changes (the order, a split, a cancel) and sets the limit; the machine keeps only the decision
    limit        : int check 0..2 = 1
    newCustomer  : bool        = false
    needsApproval: bool        = false
    approved     : bool        = false
    charged      : bool        = false
    // the carrier booking: how many were made, how many a person said did not happen, how many the host allows, and
    // whether a person found the last one
    bookings     : int check 0..2 = 0
    notFound     : int check 0..2 = 0
    maxBookings  : int check 0..2 = 2
    found        : bool        = false
    // the obligations are settling: a doubt was raised, or a part put back on track, and the answer has not come. Nothing
    // new starts meanwhile, so no message from one round overtakes the next.
    pending      : bool        = false
  }

  terminal st in { Done, Cancelled, Stuck }

  action Place(wanted: int check 2..2 disclosed, total: int check 1..2 disclosed, isNew: bool)
  action Reserved(got: int check 0..2 disclosed)
  action Substituted(got: int check 0..2 disclosed)
  action Substitute()
  action ConfirmSubstitute(by: GrantSource)
  action Split()
  action Move()
  action Agree(by: GrantSource, total: int check 0..2 disclosed)
  action Decline(by: GrantSource)
  action Cancel(n: int check 1..2 disclosed, total: int check 1..2 disclosed)
  action Picked(by: GrantSource)
  action SlotBooked()
  action BookRefused()
  action BookUnknown()
  action Resolve(exists: bool, by: GrantSource)
  action Handover(by: GrantSource)
  action Invoiced()
  action InvoiceFailed()
  action Approve(by: GrantSource)
  action Charged()
  action ChargeFailed()
  action Received(by: GrantSource)
  action Warned()

  // Ana says go: the warehouse reserves the units, and the main obligation and the picking start.
  on Place(wanted, total, isNew) {
    require st == Placed else reject "not-placed"
    require wanted > 0 else reject "nothing-to-ship"
    st' = Reserving
    qty' = wanted
    newCustomer' = isNew
    needsApproval' = isNew || total > limit
    if stock != none {
      send stock <- Reserve(from: self, qty: wanted, substitute: false)
    }
    if main != none {
      send main <- Go()
    }
    if pick != none {
      send pick <- Go()
    }
  }

  // The units reserved from the model ordered (the first time, or after the date moved). Fewer than ordered: the
  // warehouse is at risk, so the main obligation is, and the sales rep chooses a path.
  on Reserved(got) {
    require st == Reserving else reject "not-reserving"
    require got <= qty - held - held2 else reject "more-than-asked"
    held' = held + got
    if held + got + held2 >= qty {
      st' = Picking
    } else {
      st' = Short
      if main != none && pick != none {
        pending' = true
        send main <- ChildDoubt(from: pick, ack: self)
      }
    }
  }

  // The units reserved from the substitute model.
  on Substituted(got) {
    require st == Reserving && path == ViaSubstitute else reject "not-substituting"
    require got <= qty - held else reject "more-than-asked"
    held2' = got
    if held + got >= qty {
      st' = Picking
      if pick != none {
        pending' = true
        send pick <- Back(ack: self)
      }
    } else {
      st' = Short
      if main != none && pick != none {
        pending' = true
        send main <- ChildDoubt(from: pick, ack: self)
      }
    }
  }

  // The obligations have settled (a part followed its parent, or is back on track with it). What waited for that starts now:
  // the stock is asked again after the date moved, the carrier is asked again after a person found no booking.
  on Warned {
    require true else reject "never"
    pending' = false
    if st == Reserving && path == ViaMove {
      if stock != none {
        send stock <- Reserve(from: self, qty: qty - held - held2, substitute: false)
      }
    } else {
      if st == Rebooking {
        st' = Booking
        bookings' = bookings + 1
        emit reserveSlot()
      }
    }
  }

  // The three paths out of a shortage. Each waits for the people it needs.
  on Substitute {
    require st == Short && path == Direct && !pending else reject "not-short"
    st' = Substituting
    path' = ViaSubstitute
  }

  on ConfirmSubstitute(by) {
    require st == Substituting && by == ByPerson else reject "needs-the-warehouse-lead"
    // the substitute is part of what the customer is owed, so it is offered to the customer first; it is reserved on their agreement
    if qty > held {
      st' = Offering
    } else {
      st' = Picking
      if pick != none {
        pending' = true
        send pick <- Back(ack: self)
      }
    }
  }

  on Split {
    require st == Short && !pending else reject "not-short"
    st' = Offering
    path' = ViaSplit
  }

  on Move {
    require st == Short && !pending else reject "not-short"
    st' = Offering
    path' = ViaMove
  }

  // The customer agrees to the split or the later date. A split ships what is held now and leaves the rest for a second
  // shipment; a later date reserves the rest again, once the stock has arrived.
  on Agree(by, total) {
    require st == Offering && by == ByPerson else reject "needs-the-customer"
    needsApproval' = newCustomer || total > limit
    if path == ViaSplit {
      qty' = held + held2
      agreedX2' = held2
      st' = Picking
      if pick != none {
        pending' = true
        send pick <- Back(ack: self)
      }
    } else {
      st' = Reserving
      if path == ViaSubstitute {
        // the customer agreed to the substitute for the units that are short: only that much of it is reserved
        agreedX2' = qty - held
        if spare != none {
          send spare <- Reserve(from: self, qty: qty - held, substitute: true)
        }
      } else {
        if stock != none && pick == none {
          send stock <- Reserve(from: self, qty: qty - held - held2, substitute: false)
        }
        if pick != none {
          pending' = true
          send pick <- Back(ack: self)
        }
      }
    }
  }

  on Decline(by) {
    require st == Offering && by == ByPerson else reject "needs-the-customer"
    st' = Short
    path' = Direct
  }

  // The customer cancels some units, or all of them. The units reserved beyond what is still ordered go back to the
  // stock they came from. An order with nothing left is Cancelled and holds nothing.
  on Cancel(n, total) {
    require st == Short || st == Offering || st == Substituting || st == Picking || st == Booked else reject "too-late-to-cancel"
    require n > 0 && n <= qty else reject "nothing-to-cancel"
    require n == qty || !pending else reject "settling"
    needsApproval' = newCustomer || total > limit
    trimmed' = true
    qty' = qty - n
    if n == qty {
      st' = Cancelled
      held' = 0
      held2' = 0
      agreedX2' = 0
      if held > 0 && stock != none {
        send stock <- Release(n: held)
      }
      if held2 > 0 && spare != none {
        send spare <- Release(n: held2)
      }
      if main != none {
        send main <- Release()
      }
      if pick != none {
        send pick <- Release()
      }
      if book != none {
        send book <- Release()
      }
      if bill != none {
        send bill <- Release()
      }
    } else {
      if held + held2 > qty - n {
        if held >= held + held2 - (qty - n) {
          held' = held - (held + held2 - (qty - n))
          if stock != none {
            send stock <- Release(n: held + held2 - (qty - n))
          }
        } else {
          held' = 0
          held2' = held2 - (held + held2 - (qty - n) - held)
          agreedX2' = held2 - (held + held2 - (qty - n) - held)
          if held > 0 && stock != none {
            send stock <- Release(n: held)
          }
          if spare != none {
            send spare <- Release(n: held + held2 - (qty - n) - held)
          }
        }
      }
      if (st == Short || st == Offering || st == Substituting) && held + held2 >= qty - n {
        st' = Picking
        if pick != none {
          pending' = true
          send pick <- Back(ack: self)
        }
      }
    }
  }

  // JJ's warehouse picked the units: the picking obligation is met by a person, and the carrier is asked, once.
  on Picked(by) {
    require st == Picking && by == ByPerson && !pending else reject "needs-the-warehouse-lead"
    st' = Booking
    bookings' = bookings + 1
    if pick != none {
      send pick <- Confirm(by: by)
    }
    emit reserveSlot()
  }

  on SlotBooked {
    require st == Booking else reject "not-booking"
    st' = Booked
  }

  on BookRefused {
    require st == Booking else reject "not-booking"
    st' = Stuck
    if main != none {
      pending' = true
      send main <- ChildDoubt(from: book, ack: self)
    }
  }

  // The booking was asked once and nothing came back. It may exist, so it is not asked again: the order waits, the
  // carrier booking is at risk (and the main obligation), and only a person's Resolve moves it on.
  on BookUnknown {
    require st == Booking else reject "not-booking"
    st' = Unknown
    if main != none {
      pending' = true
      send main <- ChildDoubt(from: book, ack: self)
    }
  }

  // A person checked the carrier's portal. Found: the booking stands. Not found: it did not happen, and the person
  // lets it be asked again (within what the host allows); otherwise the order waits for a person.
  on Resolve(exists, by) {
    require st == Unknown && by == ByPerson && !pending else reject "needs-a-person"
    if exists {
      st' = Booked
      found' = true
      if book != none {
        pending' = true
        send book <- Back(ack: self)
      }
    } else {
      notFound' = notFound + 1
      if bookings < maxBookings {
        if book != none {
          st' = Rebooking
          pending' = true
          send book <- Back(ack: self)
        } else {
          st' = Booking
          bookings' = bookings + 1
          emit reserveSlot()
        }
      } else {
        st' = Stuck
        if main != none {
          send main <- Stall()
        }
      }
    }
  }

  // The goods leave with the carrier: a person hands them over. The booking obligation is met, and finance invoices.
  on Handover(by) {
    require st == Booked && by == ByPerson && !pending else reject "needs-the-warehouse-lead"
    st' = Invoicing
    if book != none {
      send book <- Confirm(by: by)
    }
    if bill != none {
      send bill <- Go()
    }
    emit invoice()
  }

  // The invoice exists. A charge above the limit, or to a new customer, waits for a person's approval; any other is made.
  on Invoiced {
    require st == Invoicing else reject "not-invoicing"
    if needsApproval && !approved {
      st' = Approving
    } else {
      st' = Charging
      emit charge()
    }
  }

  on InvoiceFailed {
    require st == Invoicing else reject "not-invoicing"
    st' = Stuck
    if main != none {
      pending' = true
      send main <- ChildDoubt(from: bill, ack: self)
    }
  }

  on Approve(by) {
    require st == Approving && by == ByPerson else reject "needs-the-approver"
    approved' = true
    st' = Charging
    emit charge()
  }

  on Charged {
    require st == Charging else reject "not-charging"
    charged' = true
    st' = Delivering
  }

  // The charge is asked once. If it fails, or its answer does not come, it is not asked again: a person looks.
  on ChargeFailed {
    require st == Charging else reject "not-charging"
    st' = Stuck
    if main != none {
      pending' = true
      send main <- ChildDoubt(from: bill, ack: self)
    }
  }

  // The customer confirms the receipt: a person, and the only thing that meets the main obligation.
  on Received(by) {
    require st == Delivering && by == ByPerson else reject "needs-the-customer"
    st' = Done
    if main != none {
      send main <- Confirm(by: by)
    }
    if bill != none {
      send bill <- Confirm(by: by)
    }
  }

  invariant substitute-only-as-agreed: held2 <= agreedX2
  invariant cancelled-holds-nothing: st == Cancelled implies (held == 0 && held2 == 0 && !charged)
  invariant done-is-charged: st == Done implies charged
  invariant charge-needs-approval: (st == Charging || charged) implies (!needsApproval || approved)
  invariant a-booking-is-asked-once-per-answer: bookings <= notFound + 1
  invariant found-means-a-booking-exists: found implies bookings > 0
  // a booking that timed out is moved on only by a person's Resolve: no late answer, no timer, no retry
  step property unknown-leaves-only-by-resolve: (pre.st == Unknown && post.st != Unknown) implies action == Resolve
  path property charge-at-most-once: count("billing.charge") <= 1

  effect reserveSlot() {
    kind "carrier.book"
    labels { egress:external }
    class irreversible
    retry { attempts 1, base 200ms, timeout 10s }
    ok -> SlotBooked()
    failed -> BookRefused()
    exhausted -> BookUnknown()
  }

  effect invoice() {
    kind "billing.invoice"
    labels { egress:external }
    class compensable
    retry { attempts 1, base 200ms, timeout 10s }
    ok -> Invoiced()
    failed -> InvoiceFailed()
    exhausted -> InvoiceFailed()
  }

  effect charge() {
    kind "billing.charge"
    labels { egress:external }
    class compensable
    retry { attempts 1, base 200ms, timeout 10s }
    ok -> Charged()
    failed -> ChargeFailed()
    exhausted -> ChargeFailed()
  }
}

// ---- Incident: an obligation to restore a service by a deadline (README, "Incidents"). ----------------------------------
// An incident is a page that must be answered, a path chosen, a fix that may need elevated access, a restore that a
// person verifies, and a close that gives the access back. What it owes is an Obligation (the SLA) and, apart from it,
// the customer updates are another (comms). Time is the host's: the demo clock fires Timeout, Expire, UpdateDue and
// UpdateLate; the check does not compare durations, it checks what may follow what. The forecast (server/forecast.mjs)
// reaches this machine only as Forecast, which records itself and sends Doubt to the SLA obligation, and nothing else.

enum IncidentState { Opened, Paging, Paged, Escalating, Unreached, Working, NeedsAccess, Fixing, Restored, Verified, Closing, Closed }

// How the service is brought back: roll back the change, wait for the engineer's fix, hand it to the secondary on-call.
enum FixPath { NoPath, Rollback, WaitFix, Secondary }

// What the forecast says about the deadline.
enum Outlook { OnTrack, Doubtful, WillMiss }

enum GrantState { Idle, Requested, Granted, Denied, Revoked, Expired }

// AccessGrant: time-limited elevated access to a system, for one incident. Only the owner's approval grants it, and it
// ends in exactly one of three ways: denied, expired at the end of its window, or revoked (when the incident closes).
// It is a service machine so that a revoke that arrives after the access has already ended is still answered.
service machine AccessGrant {
  state {
    st         : GrantState    = Idle
    approvedBy : GrantSource   = NoGrant
    used       : bool          = false
    inc        : Ref<Incident> = none
    // a revoke reached a grant that had already ended; it changed nothing (a write, so the no-op is visible)
    late       : bool          = false
  }

  action Request()
  action Approve(by: GrantSource)
  action Deny(by: GrantSource)
  action Use()
  action Expire()
  action Revoke(ack: Ref<Incident>)

  on Request {
    require st == Idle else reject "asked-already"
    st' = Requested
  }

  // Only the owner of the data grants access: no policy, no agent.
  on Approve(by) {
    require st == Requested && by == ByPerson else reject "needs-the-owner"
    st' = Granted
    approvedBy' = by
    if inc != none {
      send inc <- AccessReady()
    }
  }

  on Deny(by) {
    require st == Requested && by == ByPerson else reject "needs-the-owner"
    st' = Denied
    if inc != none {
      send inc <- AccessDenied()
    }
  }

  on Use {
    require st == Granted else reject "not-granted"
    used' = true
  }

  // The end of the approved window.
  on Expire {
    require st == Granted else reject "not-granted"
    st' = Expired
  }

  // The incident is closing: the access is given back, whatever its state, and the incident is told. Total, since the
  // window may have ended first.
  on Revoke(ack) {
    require true else reject "never"
    if st == Granted || st == Requested || st == Idle {
      st' = Revoked
    } else {
      late' = true
    }
    if ack != none {
      send ack <- Revoked()
    }
  }

  invariant granted-by-the-owner: st == Granted implies approvedBy == ByPerson
  liveness access-ends-with-its-window: st == Granted leads to st == Expired || st == Revoked under fair { Expire }
}

machine Incident {
  state {
    st         : IncidentState    = Opened
    path       : FixPath          = NoPath
    fc         : Outlook          = OnTrack
    // the SLA obligation, the customer-update obligation and the access grant
    main       : Ref<Obligation>  = none
    comms      : Ref<Obligation>  = none
    grant      : Ref<AccessGrant> = none
    // the page was answered (the pager's completions can arrive in any state, see PageSent)
    answered   : bool             = false
    escalated  : bool             = false
    // how many times the owner refused the access
    denied     : int check 0..2   = 0
    // a person verified that the service is back
    verified   : bool             = false
    // a customer update is owed, and one was ever late
    updateOwed : bool             = false
    lateSeen   : bool             = false
    // how many times the forecast, and a late update, have raised a doubt, and how many the configuration lets them. A
    // parameter like maxReroutes: the host sets it high, a configuration sets it small so the messages in transit stay
    // within the bound.
    doubts     : int check 0..2   = 0
    lates      : int check 0..2   = 0
    maxDoubts  : int check 0..2   = 2
  }

  terminal st in { Closed, Unreached }

  action Go()
  action PageSent()
  action PageFailed()
  action Ack()
  action Timeout()
  action Escalated()
  action EscalateFailed()
  action Choose(p: FixPath)
  action AccessReady()
  action AccessDenied()
  action FixDone()
  action Verify(by: GrantSource)
  action Close()
  action Revoked()
  action Forecast(risk: Outlook)
  action UpdateDue()
  action UpdatePosted()
  action UpdateLate()

  // The lead approved the plan: the on-call engineer is paged, once.
  on Go {
    require st == Opened else reject "not-opened"
    st' = Paging
    emit page()
  }

  // The pager's answers can arrive after the engineer's acknowledgement, so these two act only while paging.
  on PageSent {
    answered' = true
    if st == Paging {
      st' = Paged
    }
  }

  on PageFailed {
    answered' = true
    if st == Paging {
      st' = Escalating
      emit escalate()
    }
  }

  on Ack {
    require st == Paging || st == Paged else reject "not-waiting"
    st' = Working
  }

  // The page went unanswered for its limit: the secondary is paged, once.
  on Timeout {
    require st == Paging || st == Paged else reject "not-waiting"
    st' = Escalating
    emit escalate()
  }

  on Escalated {
    require st == Escalating else reject "not-escalating"
    st' = Working
    escalated' = true
  }

  on EscalateFailed {
    require st == Escalating else reject "not-escalating"
    st' = Unreached
  }

  // The lead chose how the service comes back. A rollback needs access to the production database: it asks the owner,
  // and only once (a refusal sends the lead back to choose another way).
  on Choose(p) {
    require st == Working && p != NoPath && (p != Rollback || (denied == 0 && grant != none)) else reject "cannot-choose"
    path' = p
    if p == Rollback {
      st' = NeedsAccess
      send grant <- Request()
    } else {
      st' = Fixing
    }
  }

  on AccessReady {
    require st == NeedsAccess else reject "not-waiting-for-access"
    st' = Fixing
  }

  on AccessDenied {
    require st == NeedsAccess else reject "not-waiting-for-access"
    st' = Working
    path' = NoPath
    denied' = denied + 1
  }

  // The service reports itself back. That is not the restore: a person verifies it.
  on FixDone {
    require st == Fixing else reject "not-fixing"
    st' = Restored
  }

  // Only a person's verification meets the SLA.
  on Verify(by) {
    require st == Restored && by == ByPerson else reject "needs-a-person"
    st' = Verified
    verified' = true
    if main != none {
      send main <- Confirm(by: by)
    }
  }

  // The incident closes when the service is verified and no customer update is owed; the access is given back first.
  on Close {
    require st == Verified && !updateOwed else reject "not-closable"
    if grant != none {
      st' = Closing
      send grant <- Revoke(ack: self)
    } else {
      st' = Closed
    }
  }

  on Revoked {
    require st == Closing else reject "not-closing"
    st' = Closed
  }

  // The forecast: it records what it said and, when it doubts the deadline, sends Doubt. It starts nothing, grants
  // nothing, and neither ends nor meets an obligation.
  on Forecast(risk) {
    require st != Closed && st != Unreached else reject "ended"
    fc' = risk
    if risk != OnTrack && doubts < maxDoubts {
      doubts' = doubts + 1
      if main != none {
        send main <- Doubt()
      }
    }
  }

  // A customer update is owed (30 minutes since the last), posted, or late (the next one is due).
  on UpdateDue {
    require st != Closed && st != Unreached && !updateOwed else reject "cannot-owe"
    updateOwed' = true
  }

  on UpdatePosted {
    require updateOwed else reject "none-owed"
    updateOwed' = false
  }

  on UpdateLate {
    require updateOwed else reject "none-owed"
    lateSeen' = true
    if comms != none && lates < maxDoubts {
      lates' = lates + 1
      send comms <- Doubt()
    }
  }

  invariant closed-means-verified: st == Closed implies verified
  invariant closed-owes-no-update: st == Closed implies !updateOwed
  path property page-at-most-once: count("pager.page") <= 1
  path property escalate-at-most-once: count("pager.escalate") <= 1
  liveness page-is-answered: st == Paging leads to st == Working || st == Unreached under fair { Timeout, PageSent, PageFailed, Escalated, EscalateFailed }

  effect page() {
    kind "pager.page"
    labels { egress:external }
    class irreversible
    retry { attempts 1, base 200ms, timeout 10s }
    ok -> PageSent()
    failed -> PageFailed()
    exhausted -> PageFailed()
  }

  effect escalate() {
    kind "pager.escalate"
    labels { egress:external }
    class irreversible
    retry { attempts 1, base 200ms, timeout 10s }
    ok -> Escalated()
    failed -> EscalateFailed()
    exhausted -> EscalateFailed()
  }
}

// Three configurations check the machines together. One holding every path at once does not fit an exhaustive check
// (it ran out of a 6 GB heap), so the question path and the reopen path have their own, and each configuration says
// what it leaves out. scripts/witness.mjs shows that the paths each one is for are reachable, so a CLEAN verdict is
// not a CLEAN verdict over a path no input reaches.

// define: grants, the gate, the queue and acceptance. One intent on the MRD and one on the PRD; the PRD is gated on
// the MRD. The MRD's owner (JJ) has the policy "publish drafts on their own"; the PRD's owner (Ben) asks, and may
// queue his PRD intent when the gate refuses it. The publish effect's completions are inputs, so both outcomes are
// explored and every grant invariant is exercised (PT12.3). A document is accepted with any GrantSource the
// environment offers, so the check shows a policy can never accept. Questions are left to define-ask.
configuration define {
  mrd : Document { down: prd }
  prd : Document { gated: true }
  r1  : Run
  r2  : Run
  i1  : Intent { run: r1, doc: mrd, autoPublish: true }
  i2  : Intent { run: r2, doc: prd }
  inputs { i1.Submit, i1.Cancel, i1.Accept, i1.Reject, i2.Submit, i2.Queue, i2.Dequeue, i2.Drop, i2.Approve, i2.Deny, i2.Accept, i2.Reject, r1.Step, r1.Ready, r1.Published, r1.PublishFailed, r2.Step, r2.Ready, r2.Published, r2.PublishFailed, r1.CallRequested, r1.CallCompleted, r1.Interrupted, r1.Resume, mrd.Accept, mrd.Reopen, mrd.Unpublish, prd.Accept }
  bounds { transit 12 }
  // publish needs a grant (it was "publish needs approval" before policies), and one invariant per grant source
  invariant mrd-publish-needs-a-grant: r1.published implies r1.grant != NoGrant
  invariant prd-publish-needs-a-grant: r2.published implies r2.grant != NoGrant
  // r1 is granted only by JJ's policy and r2 only by Ben: define-ask checks a person's grant on the MRD run
  invariant policy-grant-was-the-owners-policy: r1.grant == ByPolicy implies i1.autoPublish
  invariant person-grant-was-approved: r2.grant == ByPerson implies i2.approved
  invariant mrd-accepted-by-a-person: mrd.st == Accepted implies mrd.acceptedBy == ByPerson
  invariant prd-accepted-by-a-person: prd.st == Accepted implies prd.acceptedBy == ByPerson
}

// define-ask: the question path. One run on the MRD asks a decision of one of two named people (Ana or Ben), who
// answer or decline in any order; its owner approves the publish. The gate, the queue and metering are left to define.
configuration define-ask {
  mrd : Document
  ana : Person
  ben : Person
  r1  : Run { maxAsk: 2 }
  i1  : Intent { run: r1, doc: mrd }
  inputs { i1.Submit, i1.Approve, i1.Deny, i1.Accept, r1.Step, r1.Ready, r1.Ask, r1.Answered, r1.Unanswered, r1.Published, r1.PublishFailed, r1.Fail, mrd.Accept }
  bounds { transit 8 }
  invariant publish-needs-a-grant: r1.published implies r1.grant != NoGrant
  invariant person-grant-was-approved: r1.grant == ByPerson implies i1.approved
  invariant only-the-asked-answers: r1.answeredBy == none || r1.answeredBy == r1.asked
  invariant only-a-person-accepts: mrd.st == Accepted implies mrd.acceptedBy == ByPerson
}

// define-reopen: the reopen path. JJ drafts the document by his policy and accepts it; Ben's intent is refused while
// the document is accepted and queued; the document is reopened, which wakes the queue. No other configuration
// reopens a document that holds a queued intent.
configuration define-reopen {
  d  : Document
  r0 : Run
  r  : Run
  i0 : Intent { run: r0, doc: d, autoPublish: true }
  i  : Intent { run: r, doc: d }
  inputs { i0.Submit, i0.Accept, i0.Drop, r0.Step, r0.Ready, r0.Published, d.Accept, d.Reopen, i.Submit, i.Queue, i.Dequeue, i.Drop, r.Fail }
  bounds { transit 8 }
  invariant reopened-queue-is-woken: (d.st == Drafted && !d.busy) implies d.queued == none
  invariant reopen-accepted-by-a-person: d.st == Accepted implies d.acceptedBy == ByPerson
}

// obligations: an obligation is met only by a person's acceptance of the document it owes, an open one always has a run
// or a person to answer, and one that is at risk or missed has reached both parties. JJ owes Ana the MRD. The run's
// failure and the document's acceptance reach the obligation as messages in any order; the debtor's go, the doubt, the
// new path, the date passing and the release are inputs. The configuration sets maxReroutes to 1, so the check covers
// one change of path and the messages in transit stay within the bound; the host sets it high and may change it again. Grants, the gate and the queue are left to define.
configuration obligations {
  ob  : Obligation { debtor: jj, creditor: ana, maxReroutes: 1 }
  jj  : Person
  ana : Person
  mrd : Document { owed: ob }
  r1  : Run
  i1  : Intent { run: r1, doc: mrd, autoPublish: true, obligation: ob }
  inputs { ob.Go, ob.Doubt, ob.Reroute, ob.Lapse, ob.Release, i1.Submit, i1.Accept, i1.Reject, r1.Step, r1.Ready, r1.Published, r1.PublishFailed, r1.Fail, mrd.Accept, mrd.Reopen }
  bounds { transit 10 }
  // The document may be reopened after the obligation is met (a later request), and the Confirm message may arrive after
  // a reopen, so the check is on the acceptance having happened and being a person's, not on the document staying accepted.
  invariant met-means-a-person-accepted-the-document: ob.st == Met implies (mrd.drafted && mrd.acceptedBy == ByPerson)
  invariant a-failed-run-leaves-someone-on-it: (i1.st == Failed && ob.st == Open) implies (ob.working || ob.asked)
}

// order-stock: two orders share one unit of stock. They cannot hold more than there was, and a cancel gives units back.
// The orders owe nothing here (no obligations): the stock is the question. Units arriving are an input.
configuration two-orders {
  stock    : Stock
  order[2] : Order { stock: stock }
  inputs   { order[*].Place, order[*].Cancel, stock.Restock }
  bounds   { transit 6 }
  invariant never-oversold: sum(order[*].held) <= init(stock.onHand) + stock.received
}

// order-short: a shortage and the paths out of it. The warehouse owes the units, as a part of the order's main obligation
// to the customer. A part at risk puts the main obligation at risk. No party is named (an obligation with none tells nobody),
// so the Told messages, which obligations checks, are not in transit here.
configuration order-short {
  stock : Stock
  spare : Stock
  main  : Obligation { maxReroutes: 1 }
  pick  : Obligation { parent: main, maxReroutes: 1 }
  order : Order { stock: stock, spare: spare, main: main, pick: pick }
  inputs { order.Place, order.Substitute, order.ConfirmSubstitute, order.Split, order.Move, order.Agree, order.Cancel, stock.Restock }
  bounds { transit 7 }
  invariant a-part-at-risk-puts-the-main-obligation-at-risk: pick.st == AtRisk implies main.st != Open
}

// order-flow: the carrier booking that may not have happened, the invoice and the charge. The effects' completions are
// inputs, so every answer (and no answer) is explored.
configuration order-flow {
  stock : Stock { onHand: 2 }
  main  : Obligation { maxReroutes: 1 }
  book  : Obligation { parent: main, maxReroutes: 1 }
  bill  : Obligation { parent: main, maxReroutes: 1 }
  order : Order { stock: stock, main: main, book: book, bill: bill, maxBookings: 2 }
  inputs { order.Place, order.Picked, order.SlotBooked, order.BookRefused, order.BookUnknown, order.Resolve, order.Handover, order.Invoiced, order.InvoiceFailed, order.Approve, order.Charged, order.ChargeFailed, order.Received }
  bounds { transit 5 }
  invariant a-part-at-risk-puts-the-main-obligation-at-risk: (book.st == AtRisk || bill.st == AtRisk) implies main.st != Open
}

// order-parts: two parts at risk together, the shortage and the carrier timeout overlapping. The shortage (the warehouse) and
// the booking are in the same order, and the order does not book before the units are picked, so the check asks whether any
// sequence of inputs puts both at risk at once. The settling step (pending) keeps one round from overtaking the next. The check
// found the one way they can overlap: a part whose reroutes are used up (the check's cap is 1) stays at risk while its
// confirmation is still in transit, and the booking goes unknown meanwhile. The host's cap is a million, so the invariant
// says what the check proves: while a part can still be rerouted, the parts are never at risk together.
configuration order-parts {
  stock : Stock
  spare : Stock
  main  : Obligation { maxReroutes: 1 }
  pick  : Obligation { parent: main, maxReroutes: 1 }
  book  : Obligation { parent: main, maxReroutes: 1 }
  order : Order { stock: stock, spare: spare, main: main, pick: pick, book: book, maxBookings: 2 }
  inputs { order.Place, order.Substitute, order.ConfirmSubstitute, order.Move, order.Agree, order.Cancel, order.Picked, order.SlotBooked, order.BookUnknown, order.Resolve, stock.Restock }
  bounds { transit 9 }
  invariant the-parts-are-not-at-risk-together-while-one-can-be-rerouted: !(pick.st == AtRisk && book.st == AtRisk && pick.reroutes < pick.maxReroutes)
  invariant a-part-at-risk-puts-the-main-obligation-at-risk: (pick.st == AtRisk || book.st == AtRisk) implies main.st != Open
}

// incident-access: the page, the choice of path, the access to the production database, the verified restore and the close.
// The owner's answers (Approve, Deny), the end of the window (Expire) and the date passing (Lapse) are inputs, and so is
// every source of an approval, so the check shows that only a person's approval grants. No party is named.
configuration incident-access {
  main  : Obligation { maxReroutes: 1 }
  grant : AccessGrant { inc: inc }
  inc   : Incident { main: main, grant: grant, maxDoubts: 1 }
  inputs { inc.Go, inc.PageSent, inc.PageFailed, inc.Ack, inc.Timeout, inc.Escalated, inc.EscalateFailed, inc.Choose, inc.FixDone, inc.Verify, inc.Close, inc.Forecast, grant.Approve, grant.Deny, grant.Use, grant.Expire, main.Lapse }
  bounds { transit 6 }
  invariant closing-gives-the-access-back: inc.st == Closed implies (grant.st != Granted && grant.st != Requested)
  invariant the-sla-is-met-only-after-a-person-verified: main.st == Met implies inc.verified
  invariant a-forecast-only-doubts: main.st != Released
}

// incident-comms: the customer updates. A late update puts the comms obligation at risk, on its own, whatever the fix is
// doing, and the incident does not close while an update is owed.
configuration incident-comms {
  main  : Obligation { maxReroutes: 1 }
  comms : Obligation { maxReroutes: 1 }
  inc   : Incident { main: main, comms: comms, maxDoubts: 1 }
  inputs { inc.Go, inc.Ack, inc.Choose, inc.FixDone, inc.Verify, inc.Close, inc.UpdateDue, inc.UpdatePosted, inc.UpdateLate }
  bounds { transit 6 }
  invariant comms-at-risk-only-for-a-late-update: comms.st == AtRisk implies inc.lateSeen
  invariant an-owed-update-keeps-the-incident-open: inc.st == Closed implies !inc.updateOwed
  liveness a-late-update-puts-comms-at-risk: inc.lateSeen leads to comms.st == AtRisk
}
